gen-righteous-gf-open-sans: Righteous looks like thin steel rod bent into letters. Open Sans follows in a smooth, sans-serif body with bulky lowercase and no clogged curves, which gives the pair its strongest quality: loud shapes next to an easy read.
gen-righteous-gf-orienta: Punchy and playful, with a rod-bent swagger. Righteous has no hairline-to-stem shift, while Orienta's hollow-reed counters and small gap between cases keep its plain sans text quiet beside it.
gen-righteous-gf-oxygen: Bowls that fill the line give Righteous a bold, bendy-wire look, with every stroke monoline from stem to end. Oxygen's lowercase nearly matches its capitals, so paragraphs read smoothly.
gen-righteous-gf-parkinsans: Parkinsans reads crisp, one stroke thickness throughout, with wide-mouthed letters that hold up even when shrunk. Righteous then supplies the bent-wire commanding heading, and its bowls fill the line while the plain sans stays out of the way.
gen-righteous-gf-pathway-extreme: Round letters drawn like bent wire make Righteous instantly recognizable. It is the one for commanding headings, while Pathway Extreme, a sans-serif with stubby ascenders and a big x-height, handles the quiet text.
gen-righteous-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear reads with an open mouth, like a pried oyster shell, and a lofty x-height that lifts every line. Under Righteous, whose heading glides like wire, a longer passage would flow easily.
gen-righteous-gf-prompt: Righteous draws a marker-nib line that ignores direction, with bowls that fill the line and a commanding, fun streak. Prompt's oversized small letters handle the rest, while Righteous earns its keep big and short.
gen-righteous-gf-pt-sans-caption: PT Sans Caption carries big-bodied lowercase with inviting, unclosed bowls. Righteous does its best work as a commanding heading with no stem modulation, while the sans-serif handles the steady reading.
gen-righteous-gf-puritan: Puritan reads rounded and clearly open to the side, with oversized e and a counters. Righteous, a skeleton outline in one fixed stroke thickness, earns its place big and short.
gen-righteous-gf-questrial: Questrial reads flat and stencil-cut, single-weight strokes under a tall band of letters with short stalks. Righteous brings the commanding, bent-rod punch up top, and this plain sans simply does the talking below.
